text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD
- Finance Minister Rudolf Edlinger admits 17 billion schillings each are still missing for the 1998 and 1999 budgets.

- The civil servants of the Finance Ministry will go on strike again next Monday in a bid to protest against government austerity measures. Police and municipal civil servants have also threatened to go on strike should spending in the public sector be reduced any further.

- Builder Strabag plans to take over the second half of builder Stuag from Bank Austria as soon as possible even before its first option runs out in 1999. The company was able to raise earnings in 1996 even though the market economy in Austria was declining. The dividend will remain constant at 25 schillings.
- Icecream production facilities of Unilever's subsidiary Unifrost are expected to be closed down in order to reduce losses.
- Austria's new telecommunications law might pass through parliament before the summer after the Council of Ministers has accepted the draft law.
- Industrial group IFE Industrie AG expects an increase in sales of 10.6 percent to 929 million schillings this year after the company reported lower sales and pre-tax losses for 1996.
- Austrian primary school students are the best in Europe in natural sciences and mathematics, a U.S. study reports. The study ranks them third worldwide behind Korea and Japan.
DIE PRESSE

- Central bank president Klaus Liebscher denies accusations by far-right Freedom Party leader Joerg Haider that the creation of the European Central Bank would mean losses of 42 billion schillings for the Austrian National Bank.
- Insurer EA-Generali and Creditanstalt plan to end all cooperation by the end of June as a result of Bank Austria's takeover of the latter.
- Federal railways company OeBB plans to invest 100 billion schillings in extending the railtrack to four tracks between Vienna and Wels, Upper Austria.
KURIER
- Social spending will be frozen, fees raised and tax allowances cancelled in a bid to find money for the next two budgets.
- Unemployment this May was the highest compared to the same periods in the 90s due to a lack of investment in infrastructure.
- Raiffeisen Zentralbank plans to start up a subsidiary in the Ukraine in spring 1998.
- GiroCredit will start a new fund to support the tourism industry soon.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- Brickmaker Wienerberger plans to invest 700 million schillings in four new production facilities in Poland.
